To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) U.S. partnerships provide access to resources that regional partnerships and sole proprietorships do not have; (2) U.S. partners provide a greater degree of management depth than do regional partners and sole proprietorships; (3) U.S. and regional partnerships are more likely to be involved in manufacturing than sole proprietorships; and (4) sole proprietorships are more likely to have a service focus than are partnerships.
The presence of a team at inception is associated with a greater likelihood of success for start-up firms.

1) the majority of Hungarian firms are started by a single founder, 2) the majority of firms started by teams are partnerships, 3) the majority of partnerships are between Hungarians and other regional partners, and 4) firms with U.S. partners are more likely to be started by a team than firms with other partners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of U.S. principals on the start-up experience in Hungary.
the impact of partnerships on start-up strategy.
the impact of U.S. partners on the new venture in Hungary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a team of partners at the start-up of a new venture is beneficial.
the more partners a new firm has the more resources it can acquire.
the presence of a team is beneficial in that it provides a firm with the ability to access resources, and the expertise needed to formulate and implement effective strategies.
